articles.title: The night watch: the YouTubers who were guardians of a shark stuck in a South Korean canal
articles.summary:
Wearing hi-vis and carrying selfie sticks, livestreamers watched over an animal that was trapped for a month and drew more than 1.6m visitors before being guided out

In

blocks.text: In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch. Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affectionately known as Bukang-i.

On Wednesday, after more than a month in the canal and at the third attempt, the shark was successfully guided out, South Korea’s oceans ministry said. Officials expect her to move into open water in time.
For the month that she was stranded, the group of self-appointed guardians took turns to protect her, patrolling the waterfront at night for visitors who might disturb the animal.

Most are YouTubers who livestreamed the waterway, where the shark became a national celebrity. They stayed up through the night, calling out anyone shining torches or lasers into the water. Some of their videos have been watched hundreds of thousands of times.

blocks.caption: Visitors watching the shark trapped in a waterway in the south-eastern port city of Busan. Photograph: Jung Yeon-Je/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: “They bring fishing lamps, or the kind of lights people use at a campsite,” said Choi Won-jin, one of the shark’s protectors. He would arrive as the lights went out along the canal and wait for the offenders Koreans online call “lantern villains”.

The shark had been marooned in the canal since 18 September. Named after Bukhang, the Korean name for the city’s North Port, and about 3 metres long, the female dusky shark was one of a species classed as endangered worldwide. More than 1.6 million visitors came to see her, the city said, at a park that used to draw about 2,000 people on a busy Saturday.

Authorities had twice tried to guide her back out to sea and failed. Until she left, the shark remained in the canal, drawing crowds by day and leaving a handful of men to keep watch after dark. They patrolled the canal’s park to check everything was in order, ate snacks as the night went by, and shared their grievances on air about the behaviour they witnessed.

“We’re ordinary members of the public,” said Choi, who has had a YouTube channel for 10 years and covers trending issues in South Korea. “So we have no choice but to put it nicely, and get them to understand as best we can.”

“Don’t, please don’t switch the torch on,” said one of them, a YouTuber who lived nearby and went by the name Na Tae-soo. Most people complied, he said. “The animal thrashes about at night because of the torches, and it’s dangerous.”

blocks.caption: Crowds flocked to the waterfront park in Busan to see the shark. Photograph: Yonhap/EPA

blocks.text: His footage captured the shark twisting sharply away from a beam of light at 2am and striking the side of the canal. The national institute of fisheries science later confirmed an abrasion on her snout and said a visitor’s torch was likely to have startled the shark into injury.

Korean media reported that 105 officials from seven agencies watched over her, with a team on standby to reach the water within three minutes. Choi disputed this, saying that after dark it was almost up to him and the others.

The waterfront was closed to the public from midnight until 5am, a restriction the YouTubers said was impossible to enforce across a park that size. One night, livestreaming from the walkway, Choi filmed a man tipping food waste into the water.
Nobody saw the shark feed, though experts said feeding could happen in an instant and sharks her size did not need to eat often.
Further attempts to free the shark had been paused on the grounds that more force would distress her.

Cooler water had been expected to prompt her to move on. Dusky sharks prefer water between 18C and 26C, the fisheries institute said. Experts put 15C as the point below which her physiological functions would start to decline, and about 11C as the point at which survival would become precarious. Busan city officials had expected the canal to reach that temperature after the middle of November.

blocks.caption: This aerial photo taken on 29 September shows South Korean coastguard boats spraying water in an attempt to guide the shark back to the sea.  Photograph: Yonhap/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The fisheries institute recorded 46 large sharks off the east coast in the first half of this year, nearly four times as many as a year earlier, which it attributed to warmer seas and more of the fish that sharks feed on.

The affection for Bukang-i has meanwhile become an industry, with a commemorative soju, a baseball mascot in a shark cape and an honorary city ambassadorship, and nearby shops reporting a surge in sales. South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, visited the canal in mid-October.
None of the shark’s guardians thought she should be forced out. Choi said the city should protect her where she was until she left of her own accord.

Kim Jong-hwan, who runs a small business, kept watch by day as well and livestreamed her almost every day. “I went to pass on information [to my followers], and after that I started observing her”, he said. “Watching her over time, with the water pumps being fired and then the nets, I came to find those things being done to her objectionable. So we ended up cheering her on.”

“She’s just an animal, and she came in by her own choice,” Kim said. “If it gets cold, if there’s no food, if the water doesn’t suit her, she’ll leave by herself. I’d like her to just be left alone, to rest there comfortably until then, and go.”

articles.title: U.S. envoy Witkoff meets with Putin in Russia amid report Musk throttled Starlink
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in a grand imperial palace on Wednesday to review new ideas on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop…

image.caption: Russian President Vladimir Putin shakes hands with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff during a meeting at the Constantine Palace in St. Petersburg, the ninth time they have met. (Gavrlil Grigorov/Sputnik/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in a grand imperial palace on Wednesday to review new ideas on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since the Second World War.
U.S. envoy praises Putin as a 'humanitarian,' after Russia releases imprisoned American

The talks in St. Petersburg in the Constantine Palace are the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, and come amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks.
The talks in Russia began with ‌a goodwill gesture from Putin — the release of a retired U.S. school teacher, Stephen Hubbard.

The 74-year-old Michigan native was first detained in April ⁠2022 over allegations he had been manning a military checkpoint in Izyum, Ukraine, where he had resided for nearly a decade. Hubbard denied the charges but was later sentenced to six years and 10 ‌months in prison.

"You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that," Witkoff said in response to Putin, who has been subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant since 2023, for the alleged unlawful deportation of children and unlawful transfer of people from Ukraine.
A first responder walks on debris at the site of an apartment building in Kyiv, which was damaged during a Russian drone strike, on Tuesday. (Gleb Garanich/Reuters)

Witkoff flew into Russia a day after ​conducting what a U.S. official called "constructive" talks in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the leaders of Finland ​and Norway and European and NATO representatives.

A real estate magnate like Trump, Witkoff had no diplomatic experience before last year. Democrats have raised concerns about the potential conflicts of interest for Witkoff and fellow envoy Jared Kushner, given their extensive global business interests.
Putin has shown few ​signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine and no NATO membership for Kyiv.
'Either the president was lying or Musk was lying'

U.S.-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel ​costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of midterm elections on Nov. 3.

Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some ⁠intelligence sharing and to its use of ⁠the Starshield military satellite system, though Zelenskyy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve ‌those issues.
Trump is siding with ‘bloody dictator’ Putin: Chrystia Freeland

Citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of the service, which is essentially a military-grade version of Starlink developed for the Pentagon.

Throttling the speed of the satellite service, according to Ukraine officials, hampers its ability to conduct strikes on Russian targets and to defend itself from Russian drones using its own interceptor drones.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Democratic Sen. Adam Schiff of California called for the Senate to compel Musk to testify under oath in the wake of the Journal's report.
"National security decisions should be made in our national security interests, and not based on the personal whim of an unstable executive," he said.

items: Why Canadian Starlink subscribers (probably) shouldn't worry about U.S interference
Starlink restrictions would hamper Ukraine's war effort. But the country can adapt, experts say

blocks.text: Musk has said any such decision is taken by the U.S. military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible but "would like to find out" who was, in Monday comments. U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday ⁠the problem lay with the terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with.
"Either the president was lying or Musk was lying, but the decision to slow down satellite speed and access has life-or-death consequences for Ukraine," said Schiff.
At least 4 killed in Ukraine
Trump remained frustrated with Zelenskyy, whom he has repeatedly rebuked and suggested needs to be replaced, in White House comments on Tuesday.
"He's going to have to want to make a deal, because I don't think his people are going to stand for it any longer," Trump told reporters on the eve of the talks in Russia.

Ukraine held back for several days last week from hitting Russian oil refineries in deference to Trump's request to help with diesel costs, but has resumed strikes after Russia showed no sign of complying. Both sides have also struck data centres.
24 hours in Kyiv: Living through Russian drone strikes
Trump has said little about Russia's far more severe attacks on Ukraine.
"Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine," he said Monday.

Trump has had an often-contentious relationship with Ukraine's president, dating back to 2019 when he was impeached, but then acquitted, for pressuring Zelenskyy for a domestic political favour to discredit rival Joe Biden in exchange for military aid for Ukraine.

In fresh fighting, two Ukrainians over 80 years old were among four killed in overnight Russian attacks that also targeted energy facilities across four regions, officials said. The senior citizens were killed just outside the northeastern city of Kharkiv, while the two other fatalities occurred in Kyiv, where a drone slammed into an apartment building.
Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said Russia had attacked power facilities in the Kyiv, Volyn, Odesa and Mykolaiv regions, as well as civilian enterprises in at least two others.

Russia's defence ministry said its forces had hit a warehouse complex used for drone storage in the central Ukrainian city of Poltava, and an electric power substation, which supplies power to Ukrainian defence and industrial sector as well as logistics centres in Kyiv. It also said it had hit a ship carrying military cargo to Ukraine heading to the port of Odesa.
The strikes are part of a mounting campaign by Moscow to knock out the Ukrainian energy grid as winter approaches.

articles.title: Sara Duterte: Marcos, lawmakers accountable for unconstitutional national budgets
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday said President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and members of Congress should be held accountable for the passage of the budget laws for 2024 and 2025, and…

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 7:31pm

Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday said President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and members of Congress should be held accountable for the passage of the budget laws for 2024 and 2025, and part of the 2026 General Appropriations Act (GAA), which were deemed by the Supreme Court as unconstitutional.

In a statement, Duterte called out the Marcos and lawmakers following the Supreme Court's ruling in relation to irregular increases in unprogrammed appropriations (UA) that exceeded the President's proposed budget.

"Ipinagtanggol ng Korte Suprema ang batas. Ngayon, panahon na upang managot sa taumbayan si Pangulong Marcos at ang mga miyembro ng Kongreso na naglapastangan at nagpakasasa sa pera na dapat ay napunta sana sa pagpapabuti ng buhay ng mga Pilipino," Duterte said.

(The Supreme Court defended our laws. Now, it's time for President Marcos and members of Congress who violated and enriched themselves to be held accountable to the people. These funds could have been used to improve the lives of Filipinos.)

In its ruling, the Supreme Court struck down the 2024 budget because of a P449.5-billion increase in unprogrammed appropriations, while the 2025 GAA was voiced because of the additional P17.99 billion for the Special Road Fund of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).
It also ruled as unconstitutional Special Provisions 1(a) and (b), Chapter XLIII of the 2026 GAA, which authorized unprogrammed appropriations.
Duterte was critical of Marcos' role in the budget process.

"Pinapasalamatan natin ang Korte Suprema sa pagpapatibay sa Konstitusyon at pagtitiyak na manaig ang batas, batay sa desisyon nito hinggil sa pagsabing unconstitutional ang General Appropriations Act noong 2024 at 2025, at ang bahagi ng GAA 2026. Ngayon, kailangang panagutan ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ang pagpasa ng isang pambansang badyet na malinaw na taliwas sa National Expenditure Program (NEP)," Duterte said.

(We thank the Supreme Court for standing by the Constitution and ensuring that the rule of law prevailed, based on its decision regarding the unconstitutionality of the 2024, 2025 and part of the GAA 2026. Now, the President has to be held responsible for the budget that clearly went beyond the NEP.)
Duterte said the President's responsibility is clear since a budget bill would not be passed into a law unless the President signs it.

"Dapat niyang sagutin kung bakit niya nilagdaan ang isang badyet na hindi naman tumutugma sa panukala ng kanyang sariling administrasyon. Ang pambansang badyet ay pera ng taumbayan, hindi kasangkapan sa pamumulitika at personal na interes ng mga nasa puwesto sa gobyerno," the vice president added.

(The President should answer why he signed a budget that is not aligned with the proposals of his administration. The national budget is the people's money, not a tool for politics and personal interests of those in government.)
GMA News Online has requested comment from Malacañang regarding Duterte's comments, but it has yet to respond as of posting time.
Earlier in the day, Malacañang said it would ask the Supreme Court to reconsider its ruling.
The Palace said Marcos was simply adhering to existing policy and could not be held liable as he was complying with the law. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: SP Gatchalian opposes gov't coordination for Bato's surrender
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday said government authorities should not be negotiating with the armed group that is supposedly protecting Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa in Mindanao.

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 7:19pm
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday said government authorities should not be negotiating with the armed group that is supposedly protecting Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa in Mindanao.
This, after Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said that authorities are seeking to negotiate dela Rosa’s turnover with an unidentified group in order to prevent a potentially violent confrontation.

“Kung armed group ito, hindi naman sila authorized na magkaroon ng armas. Dapat hindi tayo nakikipag-negotiate sa kanila dahil hindi naman sila pwedeng mas armado pa kumpara sa gobyerno,” Gatchalian said in an ambush interview.
(If this is an armed group, they are not authorized to possess weapons. We shouldn’t be negotiating with them, because they certainly shouldn’t be more heavily armed than the government.)

“I don't know the details of itong grupo na ito. Pero ang unang iniisip ko is kung armado sila, ‘di naman sila authorized na magkaroon ng armas dahil gobyerno lang pwedeng mag-authorize sa kanila. Dapat hindi tayo nakikipag-negotiate dito sa grupong ito,” he added.

(I don’t know the details of this group. But my initial thought is that if they are armed and they aren’t authorized to possess weapons, since only the government can grant such authorization, then we shouldn’t be negotiating with them.)
Nevertheless, the Senate President said he understands where Remulla is coming from and will just leave the strategy to him.
Remulla earlier explained that authorities are trying to negotiate and resolve the matter in a “peaceful and humane way” to prevent loss of thousands of lives.
“In exchange for up to 10,000 potential deaths, I would rather negotiate first than cost the lives of Filipinos in this,” the DILG chief said.
He, however, did not give an explanation as to how he arrived at the figure or what basis he had for his estimate.
Malacañang’s call

Gatchalian also did not give a direct answer if he would echo the statement of Malacañang for Dela Rosa to surrender and face the arrest warrant issued against him by the International Criminal Court (ICC) to prevent bloodshed.
He said what matters is that the entire process would just be as peaceful as possible.
“Ang importante dito maging peaceful at maayos itong situation na ito. Ayaw natin na magkaroon ng insidente o ng aksidente,” Gatchalian said.
(What’s important here is that the situation will be peaceful and orderly. We don’t want any incidents or accidents to occur.)
Dela Rosa has been issued an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court in relation to the drug war of former president Rodrigo Duterte, which supposedly killed thousands of people.
Duterte is already detained at the ICC in The Hague, Netherlands, while awaiting his crimes against humanity trial. — BAP, GMA News

articles.summary: The complaints stem from a June 2025 report by the DICT Internal Audit Unit, which flagged possible conflicts of interest involving the hiring of former Multisys personnel as well as the awarding of…

DICT's Facebook Page

items: The Office of the Ombudsman has ordered the preventive suspension of DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr. for six months due to alleged conflicts of interest involving government contracts worth approximately P1.55 billion.

The complaints arose from a June 2025 internal audit report that flagged potential conflicts related to hiring former Multisys personnel and awarding contracts to companies with financial ties to Multisys, which Almirol founded.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman has ordered the preventive suspension of Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Undersecretary for e-Government David Almirol Jr. for alleged conflicts of interest involving government contracts worth approximately P1.55 billion.

The Ombudsman said on Wednesday, October 21, that it “found sufficient grounds to place Almirol under preventive suspension for six months without pay pending the resolution of administrative complaints of Grave Misconduct, Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service, and violation of Republic Act No. 6713 or the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.”
A preventive suspension is a cautionary measure undertaken to help ensure impartial and unimpeded investigation proceedings.

In this case, the complaints stem from a June 2025 report by the DICT Internal Audit Unit, which flagged possible conflicts of interest involving the hiring of former Multisys personnel as well as the awarding of contracts to other related companies.
Rappler reported on this issue in December 2025, citing the internal audit report of the DICT dated June 5, 2025, and our own review of Multisys’ Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings.

“It is a known fact that Undersecretary David Almirol is the founder and former Chief Executive Officer of Multisys Technologies Corporation, a privately held software engineering and digital solutions firm,” the audit report said.
The audit report also said “a conflict of interest may arise” in the following circumstances: in hiring ex-Multisys personnel and in awarding contracts to ePLDT.

According to the Ombudsman, the investigation revealed “at least 8 DICT contracts were awarded to companies with financial relationships with Multisys,” which totaled about P1.55 billion and ranged from ICT consultancies, e-government application deployment, web-based messaging services, cloud infrastructure, and data center colocation to software subscriptions.
Multisys’ audited financial statements showed revenues from the related companies “for managed services of P110.8 million in 2023 and P514.6 million in 2024.”

At the time of Rappler’s report, Almirol disputed the audit’s findings, claiming other service providers of equal or similar size such as Globe and Converge had also received contracts comparable to PLDT’s.
Conflicting SEC filings also pointed to Almirol not divesting from his Multisys business interests immediately or within the 60-day period from assuming office following his appointment to the DICT.

“Multisys’ General Information Sheet (GIS) notarized on 27 October 2022 and received by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 2 November 2022 showed that respondent was still listed as a stockholder of Multisys holding 49.21% of the stocks,” the order said.

The Ombudsman, in its preventive suspension order, noted that Almirol’s continued stay in office “could prejudice the investigation, particularly given his control and custody of documents and evidence relevant to the case.”
The Ombudsman’s order is immediately executory. The suspension will stay in effect until the administrative adjudication is completed. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: Witkoff announced this morning that Russia authorities had freed Hubbard, the first American known to be convicted of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine.

Hubbard, who grew up in Michigan, had been living with his Ukrainian wife in the eastern Ukrainian city of Izyum. He was arrested when the Russians briefly took over the city at the start of the war in 2022.

In 2024, he was sentenced to nearly seven years in prison by a Russian court. But he has always denied being involved with any combat or military unit, saying that the Russians just took him from his house.
Trump yesterday had flagged Hubbard’s release saying he’d spoken with Putin in regards to the 74-year-old. “It’s time to have Mr Hubbard back,” he said.
Opening summary
Good morning and welcome to our coverage of US politics. With 14 days until the mid-terms, we’re heading into the final straight.
President Donald Trump attended a rally last night in North Carolina, where Democrat Roy Cooper is leading Trump’s pick Michael Whatley by a considerable margin.
Undaunted though, Trump said the pollsters “never poll us right” and he predicted “some amazing results”. He’s got another rally in South Carolina later Wednesday.

Overnight he’s also posted on data centers – saying that companies building the energy-intensive sites should pay a “dividend” to the communities where they’re located, including several proposed warehouses in Michigan, where the president will head to on the weekend.

blocks.caption: Trump at a campaign rally at Pitt-Greenville Airport in Greenville, North Carolina, on Tuesday night. Photograph: Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Trump has been pushing rapid AI expansion but in a nod to how unpopular these water and electricity-guzzling centres are with locals who have to live near them, he’s been hinting at community benefits.
Trump said the “new and giant” centers “are mandated by me to make their own electricity , and ‌give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid”.

Meanwhile US envoy Steve Witkoff is in St Petersburg for a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Ukraine; some earlier wrangling by Trump has succeeded in the release of US schoolteacher Stephen Hubbard, who was captured by the Russians and accused of having fought for Ukraine.
Stay with us for all the day’s developments.

Quebec's new Parti Québécois government will officially unveil which ministers will hold key roles in cabinet on Wednesday — as the swearing-in ceremony for the PQ ministers and the province's next premier, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, begins at 1:30 p.m. at the National Assembly.

Chicoutimi MNA Marie-Karlynn Laflamme will take on the role of Minister of Health, Prevention and Seniors. She was elected in a by-election in February 2026 and is one of ten caucus members who have already served in the National Assembly.

items: New government, lots of new faces: Get to know some of Quebec's newest MNAs

blocks.text: It will be her responsibility, among other things, to abolish Santé Québec, as promised by the PQ leader.

Arseneau, the MNA for the the Magdalen Islands, will become Minister of Education. He's served in opposition since 2018, making him one of the most experienced members of the PQ caucus. Nicolas Marceau will become Minister of Finance, which was his former role under Pauline Marois' government between 2012 and 2014.

Veteran politician Alain Therrien, another former PQ member who is making a return to the National Assembly after serving in Ottawa for the Bloc Québécois from 2019 to 2025, will be appointed President of the Treasury Board and Minister responsible for Government Administration.
Sources say St-Pierre Plamondon's cabinet will have 22 ministers, 23 including himself. That's six fewer than Christine Fréchette's cabinet.

items: What to expect from a Parti Québécois government

blocks.text: The PQ was elected to form a minority government on Oct. 5, four years after only winning three seats in the 2022 provincial election. This time, the party won 59 out of 127 seats, falling five short of a majority.
The 59 MNAs were sworn in last Thursday. MNAs for the Quebec Liberal Party and Québec Solidaire were sworn in this week.
The ceremony for the 19 MNAs of the Conservative Party of Quebec is Thursday.
Constitutional challenge looms over ceremony
Wednesday's ceremony will be historic. It will unfold against the backdrop of a constitutional challenge.
It will be the first time that the lieutenant-governor — a representative of the monarchy — will not preside over the swearing-in ceremony of a new government's cabinet at the National Assembly.

items: Lieutenant-governor will skip Quebec cabinet's swearing-in at incoming premier's request

blocks.text: The ceremony also comes a day after court hearings at the Montreal courthouse.

A constitutional lawyer argued that a provincial law passed in 2022 that abolished the requirement to pledge allegiance to the King creates a situation where MNAs would be sitting inside the National Assembly unlawfully.

items: Renouncing oath to the King threatens National Assembly's legitimacy, lawyer argues

blocks.text: The lawyer is asking the Superior Court to issue a stay and force MNAs to take the oath between now and Nov. 17, when the National Assembly is expected to reconvene.
A decision is expected in the next month.

articles.title: ASEAN declaration aims for safe, fair recruitment of migrant workers --DMW
articles.summary: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is crafting a declaration that calls for stronger regional action against fraudulent online recruitment and safer migration amid the prevalence of…

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 6:37pm

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is crafting a declaration that calls for stronger regional action against fraudulent online recruitment and safer migration amid the prevalence of human trafficking across the region, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Wednesday.

The Declaration on the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Migrant Workers (ACMW) provides an operational framework for member states to address emerging challenges like cyber-enabled recruitment fraud, safe migration pathways, and worker protection guidelines.
"Very relevant sa atin [dahil] may cases ng scam hubs [na biktima] ang mga kabayan natin," DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said during the Kapihan sa Manila Bay forum.
(The declaration is very relevant because we have cases of scam hubs that victimized our countrymen.)
According to Cacdac, the government has so far repatriated 3,000 Filipino victims of scam hubs, some of whom are victims of sex trafficking.
"May law enforcement effort dito ang ASEAN member states to curb itong mga scam hubs, scam farms na tinatawag," Cacdac said.
(The ASEAN member states have law enforcement efforts to curb the scam hubs and scam farms.)
The DMW secretary attributed the prevalence of human trafficking in ASEAN countries to the visa-free jurisdiction in the region.
"Malamang sa malamang itatawid 'yan sa isang visa-free jurisdiction, dun muna sila dadalhin. And then from there, isasakay na sila sa mga fishing boats," Cacdac said.
(Victims are most likely to traverse a visa-free country, then will sail in a fishing boat to their destination.)
With this scheme, ASEAN member states strenghtened it coordination and tighten its borders security.
"On the same page, ang mga ASEAN member states ay magkakaroon ng pagkakaintindihan na ipagbawal ang illegal recruitment," Cacdac said.
(The ASEAN member states are on the same page in prohibiting illegal recruitment.)
"That is why we have tight coordination across ASEAN and within our country with law enforcement," he added.

The Philippines, through DMW, led the 19th ASEAN Forum on Migrant Labour (AFML) this month, where member states discussed the growing threat of cyber-enabled recruitment schemes and how to address it. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Pakistan-Taliban conflict: How India could benefit from shifting regional dynamics
articles.summary: As Pakistan's influence in Afghanistan comes under strain, India is rebuilding ties with the Taliban in Kabul. Can New Delhi turn this diplomatic opening into lasting strategic gains?

image.caption: Clashes between Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban erupted in early 2026 [FILE: March 19, 2026]Image: Abdul Basit/AFP

blocks.text: Pakistan and Afghanistan right now are locked in a cycle of escalating tension. Repeated border clashes have strained ties between Islamabad and Kabul.

The current round of tensions began in February 2026, when Pakistan launched strikes into Afghanistan targeting Taliban militants. At one point in March, Pakistan's defense minister said the country was at "open war" with Afghanistan. Periodic bouts of violence have continued since then, with the latest Pakistani strikes targeting the Afghan Taliban's "terrorist hubs" reported earlier in October.

At the heart of the dispute is Pakistan's accusation that the Taliban authorities in Kabul allow the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), a militant group, to target Pakistan from Afghan territory. Kabul denies providing the group with sanctuary.
Militants kill dozens of security officers in Pakistan
Where does India come into play?

As the two neighbors trade strikes, the escalating conflict "presents a significant diplomatic and strategic opportunity for India," Shanthie Mariet D'Souza, an Afghanistan expert and founder of the India-based Mantraya Institute for Strategic Studies, told DW.
D'Souza argues the confrontation has weakened Pakistan's traditional influence in Kabul and encouraged the Taliban to broaden its external relations.

"India can respond by expanding diplomatic engagement, humanitarian assistance, development projects and trade, while seeking assurances that Afghan territory will not be used by anti-India militant groups," she said.
However, D'Souza cautioned against interpreting the opening as a fundamental realignment.

"There is no ideological alignment between India and the Taliban," she said. Afghanistan under Taliban rule is likely to pursue a diversified foreign policy rather than align exclusively with New Delhi.

India also lacks the geographical advantages, economic leverage and security presence needed to replace Pakistan's influence, she notes. "The scenario of the Taliban becoming a strategic ally remains far-fetched."
Former Indian ambassador to Afghanistan Amar Sinha warned against viewing the conflict simply as an opportunity for New Delhi to gain at Pakistan's expense.

"The issues have very little to do with India," Sinha told DW, arguing that India was not seeking strategic advantage from the fighting. He also pointed to the consequences of Pakistan's military actions for Afghan civilians.
"Yet the rupture has made Kabul's search for alternative partners more pressing," he added.

For New Delhi, that creates an opening, but not necessarily a strategic alignment, Sinha notes. The Taliban can seek Indian assistance while maintaining relations with China, Russia, Iran and Gulf states, preserving its autonomy rather than exchanging dependence on Pakistan for dependence on India.
The cost of closer ties

Gautam Mukhopadhyaya, another former Indian ambassador to Afghanistan, sees the deterioration in relations between Pakistan and the Taliban as an opportunity for India to recover some of the strategic ground it lost when the Taliban returned to power in 2021.
"The crisis has allowed strategic openings for India," Mukhopadhyaya told DW, warning that New Delhi's own treatment of Afghans could undermine its efforts to build a durable relationship.
He pointed to restrictions affecting Afghans seeking Indian visas for education, scholarships, work and medical treatment.
"For all practical purposes, India's security establishment treats Afghans as proxy Pakistanis and 'terrorists' by default," he said.
Former Afghan partners had been left "disappointed, even bitter," Mukhopadhyaya added. "A strategic relationship built on the sands of oppression is not a sound foundation."
'Don't send us back': Afghan women in India fear deportation
Trade cannot overcome geography
India has restored air freight links between Kabul and Delhi and between Kabul and Amritsar in December 2025.
Bilateral trade between India and Afghanistan stood at about $908 million in the 2025-26 fiscal year, while trade between Pakistan and Afghanistan fell sharply amid repeated border closures.

On October 14, Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi stressed the importance of relations with India during talks with Indian charge d'affaires Yatin Patel, signaling Kabul's interest in expanding economic cooperation.
But air freight is expensive, and India cannot easily replace Pakistan as a transit route.
New Delhi has sought to use Iran's Chabahar port to improve access to Afghanistan and Central Asia, but regional instability and complications surrounding Iran have constrained those ambitions.
D'Souza cautioned that "the ongoing conflict in Iran" limits India's ability to use Chabahar as a crucial trade and connectivity hub.
Gulshan Sachdeva, a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University specializing in Afghanistan and Eurasian connectivity, highlighted similar obstacles.

"In the last few decades, Islamabad has obstructed Kabul's efforts to gain access to the vast Indian market. However, political instability in Afghanistan and sanctions on Iran have undermined these efforts," Sachdeva told DW.
"Afghanistan's potential as a connector between regional markets remains considerable, but the infrastructure and political conditions needed to realize it are far from assured," he added.

Sachdeva also sees Russia and China as better positioned to shape Afghanistan's wider economic integration. Alternative routes may become more attractive to India, but they are not commercially viable overnight.
Islamabad's security fears

Pakistan has portrayed arch-rival India's growing engagement with the Taliban as a security threat. On October 7, Pakistani diplomat Muhammad Jawad Ajmal accused India at the United Nations of providing the Taliban with material and logistical support.
"Under the guise of humanitarian aid, they have been actively supporting the Taliban regime with material and logistical support for carrying out terrorist attacks against Pakistan," Ajmal said.
The allegation reflects Islamabad's position and has not been established as fact.
Pakistan has accused India of supporting the TTP and the Balochistan Liberation Army, a militant organization.
India rejects accusations of backing militant activity, while the Taliban denies allowing Afghan territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.
Ayesha Siddiqa, a Pakistani expert on military and security affairs at King's College London, offered a more nuanced assessment of Pakistan's position.
"India has stepped into a space and is trying to exert its influence and feed anti-Pakistan groups intelligence," she told DW.
Siddiqa added that Pakistan's establishment continues to view the crisis through "a singular security lens."
"Islamabad feels physically squeezed from both sides," she said, adding that closer Kabul-New Delhi ties could create "a dangerous two-front security trap" for Pakistan.
India may gain more room to operate in Afghanistan as ties between Kabul and Islamabad deteriorate. But the Taliban is unlikely to put all its eggs in New Delhi's basket.
Why Pakistan is fighting the Taliban it once backed

articles.title: Government trying to take VP Sara down? Palace calls claim laughable
articles.summary: The Palace on Wednesday thumbed down Vice President Sara Duterte"s claim that the government had a strategy to take her down.

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 6:34pm
The Palace on Wednesday thumbed down Vice President Sara Duterte’s claim that the government had a strategy to take her down.
Duterte earlier claimed that there was an attempt from the government to frame her issues as a matter of national security.

“Habang binabasa ko siya kanina, ako ay lubhang natawa. Nakakatawa dahil kabalintunaan ang kanyang mga sinasabi dito sa kanyang statement na may petsang October 20, 2026. Bakit nakakatawa? Pinag-uusapan dito ang patungkol sa may bandang dulo ay start working and stop politicking,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said in a media briefing.

(While I was reading it earlier, I was wholly laughing. It is funny because what she is saying here in her statement dated October 20, 2026 is ironic. Why is it laughable? She said here at the end to start working and stop politicking.)

“Kahit na nasa gitna tayo ng krisis ng Middle East, maraming kalamidad na humarap sa atin at sa ngayon ay may El Niño. Nandiyan ang Pangulo, hindi lang para managot ang dapat na managot, nagsusumikap, nagtatrabaho, pinapatupad ang batas para managot ang dapat na managot—isama na pati ang mga nagtatraydor sa bansa,” Castro said.

(Even if we are in the middle of the crisis in the Middle East, there are a lot of calamities in front of us and now where is the El Niño. The President is there, not just to hold the responsible to account, to try hard, to work, to implement the law to hold people into account—including those betraying the country.)
It was Duterte who has had several personal foreign trips, Castro said.

The Palace exec urged the public not to be distracted. While the Palace will not intervene with Duterte’s ongoing impeachment trial at the Senate, she maintained that the prosecution has presented a lot of evidence. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Reader Q&A: What’s next for France after a weekend of riots? Ask our Europe columnists
articles.summary: At 3pm BST / 4pm CEST Friday 23 Oct, Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst will be live taking questions from our readers about the riots and protests in…
articles.byline: Rokhaya Diallo, Alexander Hurst, Michael Hubbard and Guardian moderators

blocks.text: Key events

items: 27m agoWelcome to the Conversation

blocks.text: Welcome to the Conversation

blocks.caption: The Hôtel de Ville in Limoges, central France, on fire during a weekend of unrest. Photograph: Pascal Lachenaud/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: After weeks of protests and a weekend of riots in which a town hall was set ablaze, 2,000-plus shops were looted, 2,300 people were arrested and 1,000 police injured, the repercussions for France – for its society and its economy – continue. Allegations of police brutality surfaced, and the violent protests unnerved investors, resulting in a debt sell-off, with borrowing costs rising higher than for Greece. All of this ahead of a hotly contested presidential election that’s now just six months away.

The French government’s escalating financial problems were covered by the Guardian’s Europe correspondent Jon Henley who wrote: “France’s national debt, at 119% of GDP, is at its highest level since 1946. Its budget deficit, at 5.1%, is also among the highest in the EU. There is just no money in the bank to ease the cost of living squeeze that brought 550,000 people on to the streets on Saturday.”

Columnist Paul Taylor commented that “Last weekend’s violence has increased the likelihood of a law-and-order backlash among voters that could propel (Marine) Le Pen into the Élysée Palace. But if the financial situation worsens and the campaign turns on who can save the economy, she may yet lose out to a candidate who is firm on security and more orthodox on fiscal policy.”

And the Guardian’s editorial noted that “In an increasingly febrile atmosphere, France is heading towards a seismic reckoning in May. Alarmingly, the civil strife witnessed at the weekend may only be a foretaste of what is to come.”

What are your views on the riots, their causes and their aftermath? Are they paving a path to the presidency for Le Pen? In his final months in charge, can embattled incumbent Emmanuel Macron meaningfully address the situation in which France finds herself?

France-based Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst will be live here at 1500BST on Friday 23 October to answer your questions on what happened, why, and where France goes from here.
Comments will open at 0900BST on Friday, but you can send your questions by email now to conversations@theguardian.com

articles.title: Ombudsman suspends DICT exec over alleged conflict of interest in P1.55B contracts
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman on Wednesday placed Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Undersecretary for E-Government David Almirol Jr. under a six-month preventive…

blocks.text: The Office of the Ombudsman on Wednesday placed Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Undersecretary for E-Government David Almirol Jr. under a six-month preventive suspension over an alleged conflict of interest involving government contracts worth around P1.55 billion.

In its seven-page order, the Ombudsman said that the suspension stemmed from the pending administrative complaints of grave misconduct, conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service and a criminal complaint for alleged violation of Republic Act No. 6713 or the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.

The complaints were based on a report by the DICT Internal Audit Unit dated June 2025 flagging a possible conflict of interest involving the hiring of former Multisys personnel and the award of contracts to other related companies, considering that Almirol founded Multisys Technologies Corporation (Multisys) in 2010.

Almirol also served as its president and chief executive officer for more than a decade before his appointment as DICT Undersecretary for E-Government in August 2022 and would later lead the development and rollout of the eGovPH Super App.

“Further investigation of the Office of the Ombudsman revealed that at least eight DICT contracts were awarded to companies with financial relationships with Multisys. From November 2023 to May 2025, the DICT awarded eight eGov-related contracts to several related companies totaling to about P1.55 billion,” the Ombudsman said.

“These contracts covered information and communications technology consultancy, e-government application deployment, web-based messaging services, cloud infrastructure, data center colocation and software subscriptions,” the Ombudsman added.

In addition, the Ombudsman said Multisys’ audited financial statements showed revenues from the related companies for managed services, and that the audited financial statements report revenue from the other companies “for managed services of P110.8 million in 2023 and P514.6 million in 2024”.
Records also showed that Almirol did not divest immediately after his appointment to the DICT. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Signal No. 2 still up in Batanes as Super Typhoon Rosal slightly weakens
articles.summary: Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 remains in effect over Batanes as Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) slightly weakened while moving west-northwestward over the sea east of Northern…

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 6:16pm
Satellite rendering shows Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) taken as of 4:30 a.m. of Oct. 21, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 remains in effect over Batanes as Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) slightly weakened while moving west-northwestward over the sea east of Northern Luzon, the state weather bureau PAGASA said Wednesday.
In its 5 p.m. bulletin on Wednesday, October 21, PAGASA said Rosal was packing maximum sustained winds of 205 kilometers per hour near the center and gusts of up to 250 kph.
The super typhoon was last spotted 725 kilometers east of Aparri, Cagayan, moving west-northwestward at 25 kph.
Strong to typhoon-force winds extend up to 780 kilometers from the center.
Warning signals
PAGASA raised the following tropical cyclone wind signals:
Signal No. 2
Luzon

items: Batanes

blocks.text: Residents in the province may experience gale-force winds ranging from 62 to 88 kph within the next 24 hours, posing minor to moderate threats to life and property.
Signal No. 1

items: Cagayan, including the Babuyan Islands
Eastern portion of Isabela (Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, Delfin Albano, Santo Tomas, Tumauini, San Pablo, Ilagan City, San Mariano, Dinapigue)
Ilocos Norte
Apayao
Northeastern portion of Catanduanes (Pandan, Bagamanoc, Panganiban, Viga, Gigmoto)

blocks.text: Residents in these areas may experience strong winds ranging from 39 to 61 kph within the next 36 hours, posing minimal to minor threats to life and property.
PAGASA said the highest wind signal that may be raised during Rosal's passage is Signal No. 3.
The northeast monsoon and Rosal's outer circulation will also bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas:

items: Wednesday, October 21: Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, Bicol Region, Romblon, Eastern Visayas, Siquijor, Bohol, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Davao Region, Aurora, Quezon and Sarangani.
Thursday, October 22: Most of Luzon and the Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Northern Mindanao, Agusan del Norte, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Sarangani, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental.
Friday, October 23: Most of Luzon and the Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental.

blocks.text: PAGASA advised the public to refer to Weather Advisory No. 5, issued at 5 p.m. Wednesday, for the heavy rainfall outlook due to Rosal.
Sea conditions
A gale warning is in effect over the northern and eastern seaboards of Luzon and the eastern seaboard of the Visayas.

Very rough seas, with waves reaching up to 10 meters, are expected along the northern and eastern seaboards of Batanes. Waves may reach up to 9 meters along the remaining seaboard of the province and the eastern seaboard of the Babuyan Islands.

Waves may reach up to 8 meters along the northern seaboard of the Babuyan Islands and the northeastern seaboard of mainland Cagayan. Seas may reach up to 7 meters along the remaining seaboards of mainland Cagayan and the Babuyan Islands, as well as the northeastern seaboard of Isabela.
Very rough seas, with waves reaching up to 6 meters, are expected along the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte and the remaining seaboard of Isabela.
Waves may reach up to 5 meters along the northern and eastern seaboards of Catanduanes, the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte and the northern seaboard of northern Aurora.

PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types of vessels in areas where very rough seas are expected. Mariners were advised to remain in port or seek shelter in a safe harbor until winds and waves subside.
Operators of small vessels, including motorbancas, were also advised against venturing out to sea under rough conditions.
Track, intensity
Rosal is expected to continue moving west-northwestward on Wednesday before turning northwestward on Thursday, October 22.
The super typhoon is forecast to turn north-northwestward by Friday, October 23, before recurving north-northeastward on Saturday, October 24.

On its forecast track, Rosal will be closest to Extreme Northern Luzon between Thursday afternoon and Friday morning before exiting the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by Friday evening or early Saturday.
PAGASA said Rosal is forecast to gradually weaken into a typhoon by Friday and continue weakening near Taiwan due to unfavorable conditions.
The weather bureau cautioned that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still affect areas outside the forecast track and that Rosal's path may still change.

articles.title: Australian MP loses both legs after alleged vehicle attack as suspect appears in court
articles.summary: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs amputated after being rammed by a car outside her electoral office, her husband said on Wednesday, as the man accused of the attack appeared in…

image.caption: Helen Haines, an independent lawmaker in Australia, was struck twice by a car on Monday outside her electoral office, Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne on Monday. (Mick Tsikas/AAP/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs amputated after being rammed by a car outside her electoral office, her husband said on Wednesday, as the man accused of the attack appeared in court.
Politician's husband says his wife is stable

Doctors amputated Haines's left leg after she was struck twice by a car in Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne, on Monday, Phil Haines said. They worked for days to save her right leg but were ultimately unsuccessful, he told a news conference in Melbourne.
"The good news in all this is Helen is alive and she's stable. That is the most important thing for our family," he said.

Brendan Nugent, a 43-year-old resident of the rural town of Tarrawingee within Haines's electorate, was charged with three offences: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a public official.
Additional charges of cannabis cultivation and possession have also been laid against Nugent, court filings showed.
Phil Haines, left, Haines's husband, speaks to reporters alongside Australia's Governor General Sam Mostyn in Melbourne. (William West/AFP/Getty Images)
The suspect was restrained by members of the public at the scene before being arrested.
Haines, an independent lawmaker who has championed causes including climate change and regional housing, remains in critical condition.
Police are still investigating the motive for the rare attack on an elected official.
Appears in court

During a brief court appearance on Wednesday, the accused's lawyer said his client suffers from a rare neurological condition called idiopathic transverse myelitis and was also being treated for concussion, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported. His lawyer told the magistrate his client had some mental health concerns and that it was his first time in custody.
There was no application for bail, and the case was deferred until Feb. 4.
Anti-terrorism police are among the agencies investigating the incident. While police allege the attack was "targeted," they say they believe it was an isolated incident.

There was no intelligence to suggest any threat to Haines, and the Australian Federal Police received no warning of any imminent danger from the alleged attacker, Commissioner Krissy Barrett told reporters.
"What I can say is we didn't have any specific intelligence that would have indicated something as atrocious as happened on Monday afternoon," she said.
Victoria state police said they could not find any direct past contact between Haines and the accused, with the motive still unknown.

"Motivation is one of these things that we absolutely need to explore. His motivation for this, what we allege is a deliberate attack, is very much a centerpiece of the investigation," Victoria Police Chief Mike Bush said.
Bush declined to comment on the man's mental health, saying the matter was before the court.

items: Man charged in vehicle attack on Australian MP

blocks.text: Haines had worked in nursing, midwifery and academia before being elected to Parliament in 2019 for the rural seat of Indi, which she retained in both 2022 and 2025.

Violent attacks on politicians are rare in Australia, where federal lawmakers, state leaders and even prime ministers are often seen shopping, grabbing coffee or attending community events with relatively little security.

However, concerns about politicians' safety have grown in recent years amid rising political polarization, online abuse and threats against elected officials, prompting calls for greater protections while preserving the accessibility that has long characterized Australian politics.

articles.title: Witness: Immigration officials named Chinese passengers cleared under pastillas scam
articles.summary: High-ranking officials of the Bureau of Immigration (BI) supplied the names of Chinese passengers who were allowed entry to the country without proper inspection in exchange for grease money, also…

blocks.text: High-ranking officials of the Bureau of Immigration (BI) supplied the names of Chinese passengers who were allowed entry to the country without proper inspection in exchange for grease money, also known as the pastillas scam, an Immigration personnel said Wednesday.

Prosecution witness and Immigration officer Allison Chiong made the testimony during the trial on the six counts of graft cases filed against former BI deputy commissioner Marc Mariñas and at least 49 others before the Sandiganbayan Seventh Division for allegedly conspiring with other Immigration personnel.

The Immigration officials also allegedly conspired with Liya Wu of Empire International Travel and Tours to "willfully, unlawfully and give unwarranted benefits, preference or advantage to foreign passengers, particularly Chinese nationals."

The group allegedly collected a fee of P10,000 per passenger, wrapped in small pieces of paper like the dessert pastillas, for a total amount of P1.43 million in violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.

Chiong, during the cross-examination of the defense counsels, said that the suppliers of the Chinese passengers’ names who are allowed entry without proper inspection were Francis Dennis “DR” Robles, Glenn Ford Silang Comia a.k.a. “Orange”, Rodolfo Magbuhos, Jr., Deon Carlo “Nancy” Albao, Danieve Hije “Den” Binsol a.k.a. “Denden”, Pauk Erick Borja and Anthony Lopez.
“They confirmed to me their aliases and contribution to the pastillas scheme. They told me [about it] and I experienced it too,” Chong told the Sandiganbayan Seventh Division.
“Upon arrival, the Chinese nationals were allowed in without being inspected,” she said.
Asked by the defense if he saw how the money was given, she said, “It is from the bosses; they give it to us.”
The defense team then clarified if Chiong saw purported Chinese “pastillas” passengers giving money to immigration officers, the witness said, No.
During the cross-examination, Chiong was also made to read portions of his judicial affidavit and his previous affidavit with three supplemental affidavits.
Chiong said that in 2016, Robles personally supervised the entry of two Chinese nationals to his counter.
“They have tourist visa, [and] it was inconsistent with their travel itinerary that they would stay only in Metro Manila,” she stated in his affidavit.
“Robles instructed me to let them pass through without secondary inspection. I followed Robles since he is my superior, I did not want to be on his bad side,” she added.
Chiong also confirmed to the defense counsel that he only alleged that Maria Victoria Jogno was involved in the pastillas scam in his judicial affidavit in 2026.

In the said affidavit, Chiong said "I (Chiong) have personally witnessed, on a regular basis, her (Jogno) processing of “pastillas” passengers because the counters assigned for the pastillas passengers are arranged adjacent to each other. The act of giving seamless entry to passengers by IOs is within the clear view of each member." —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: [DECODED] You no longer have to click anything to be targeted. But you can fight back.
articles.summary: With today's technological advances, malicious actors have found a way to get consumer data without you clicking on anything

blocks.text: With today's technological advances, malicious actors have found a way to get consumer data without you clicking on anything

items: The Cambridge Analytica scandal in 2018 revealed that the firm improperly accessed data from over 87 million Facebook users to target them for political campaigns, using tactics like viral quizzes to gather personal information.

Recent reports indicate that malicious actors, such as the Israeli firm Discover-Tech, have developed new methods to spy on users through online ads without requiring any user interaction, highlighting a shift in data privacy threats.

Maria Ressa's book, 'The Fight Back,' offers strategies for individuals and institutions to combat disinformation and protect democracy in the age of AI, emphasizing the importance of active engagement in data protection.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Remember when the Cambridge Analytica scandal blew up in 2018? It’s the data harvesting scandal that took place around 2014, where Cambridge Analytica had improperly accessed — and sold — the data of Facebook users to target them for political campaigns. Cambridge Analytica was a British political consultancy that worked for Donald Trump’s 2016 election campaign.

Facebook later reported that Cambridge Analytica had harvested personal data of over 87 million users, over 1.1 million of which were Filipinos. The data obtained included users’ phone numbers and contact lists, which allowed them to target not just the users who fell prey to the operations, but also their contacts who weren’t necessarily on their Facebook network.

How did they do it? Well, they had to be creative. They used those viral personality quizzes that tricked users into sharing details about themselves, perhaps convincing them that it was all in good fun. In reality, the firm used these details to profile, segment, and micro-target them for political campaigns.

Targeted advertising has been found to create isolation and division among consumers by limiting their exposure to diverse viewpoints and feedback — hence reinforcing what we now call “echo chambers.”
That happened over a decade ago. So much has changed in our information landscape since then, and malicious actors have gained other tools beyond social media platforms.
What if I told you that, with today’s technological advances, malicious actors have found a way to get consumer data without you clicking on anything?

Just last week, reports said that an Israeli digital advertising agency called Discover-Tech gave access to Candiru, a spyware company blacklisted by the US government, to advertising platforms run by Google, Comcast, and Russia’s Yandex. By doing so, Candiru was able to spy on internet users through a wide network of online ads, which only needed to load on the user’s side for the spying to occur. No clicks needed!

Two research groups, Citizen Lab and Confiant, separately investigated Discover-Tech and said that it utilized its data-sharing arrangements called cookie matching to track people. The researchers also said that some of its ads were used to help “plant spyware” on users’ devices.

Granted, the researchers said that the ads they found to be tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech’s overall volume. But the point stays the same: unlike the Cambridge Analytica scandal where users had to be coaxed into taking quizzes, there is now evidence that users don’t even have to do anything to be targeted by malicious actors. Simply being served an ad could be enough to compromise their personal details.

You might think that this is a problem for other countries, not for the Philippines. But recall that Cambridge Analytica had used the Philippines as a “petri dish” to test out its strategies before rolling it out to Western countries, thanks to our high social media usage and lack of regulation.

If you find this scary or at least alarming (like I do), Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Rappler CEO Maria Ressa’s new book, The Fight Back: A Citizen’s Guide to Standing Up to Dictators, is a good place to start.

In The Fight Back, Maria draws on her years on the frontlines against disinformation and Big Tech overreach and discusses in detail what citizens and institutions can do to understand, defend, and rebuild democracy in the age of AI.

She lays out 10 strategic goals across 10 chapters, each broken down into 10 concrete actions, to help people reclaim control over the technologies now shaping our lives — from mapping the battlefield and defending our communities to building a world where technology works for the people, not against us.
Maria discussed these and more in a conversation with WNYC’s Brian Lehrer for the second edition of Democracy Dialogues on October 16. You can watch Maria’s full interview here.

I hope this newsletter spooked you enough to take a more active role in protecting your own data and digital life. October, after all, is not only about Halloween. October is also cybersecurity awareness month. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Palace: China envoy spat could be a distraction from Duterte probe
articles.summary: Malacañang on Wednesday reiterated that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. is not backing down in the country"s claim in the West Philippine Sea (WPS), saying that any heated discussion should…

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 5:45pm

Malacañang on Wednesday reiterated that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. is not backing down in the country’s claim in the West Philippine Sea (WPS), saying that any heated discussion should not distract from a key issue at hand: Vice President Sara Duterte allegedly accepting foreign funds.

Chinese Envoy to the Philippines Jing Quan garnered widespread criticisms from various Philippine officials and government agencies after he seemingly threatened Manila with Beijing’s military force should tensions escalate in the WPS.

“Ang nais lang natin muna ay sa mga ganitong maiinit na palitan ng mga salita, huwag din tayong maligaw. May issue pa tayong dapat na kaharapin. Kung totoo bang nagbibigay ng pondo ang ibang bansa sa Bise Presidente,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a media briefing.
(What we want is that, with these heated exchanges, let us not get lost. We have an issue we need to face. If it is true that the Vice President was given money by another country.)

“Baka dahil sa ingay na ito, naliligaw tayo, nililigaw tayo. So huwag nating kalimutan na dapat pa maimbestigahan ang isyu na ito dahil kapag nagkaroon ng katotohanan ito, tama ang Bise Presidente na issue ito ng national security,” she added.

(Maybe with this noise, we are getting lost. So let us not forget that this issue needs to be investigated because once the truth gets found out, the Vice President is right that this could be a national security issue.)
Asked if Castro was implying that Quan’s issue was being used as a smokescreen for Duterte, the Palace exec said it was best for the public to judge.
However, she said that while there are statements that need to be answered, there are still matters that need to be confronted.
Not backing down
Lawmakers from both chambers of Congress have already filed separate resolutions urging Marcos to declare Quan persona non grata.
Senator Francis "Kiko" Pangilinan had challenged Marcos to send the “hooligan” Quan back home. Asked about Pangilinan’s plea to Marcos, Castro maintained that Marcos was not backing down on the WPS.

“Ang nais ng Pangulo, unang-una ay walang umagaw sa ating teritoryo, malinaw iyan. Ayaw ng Pangulo, na mayroon umagaw sa interes sa West Philippine Sea, malinaw iyan. Hindi po iyan inaabandona ng Pangulo. Tuloy-tuloy ang pagpapalakas ng ating puwersa para tuloy-tuloy ang pagprotekta sa ating teritoryo at maritime rights,” Castro said.

(What the President wants, first off, is to make sure no one steals our territory, that is clear. The President does not want anyone to steal our interests in the West Philippine Sea, that is clear. The President did not abandon that. Efforts continue to strengthen our forces to protect our territory and maritime rights.)
Quan and the Chinese Embassy have openly been argumentative with various government officials following the envoy’s comments.
The Chinese Embassy had even published a list of lawmakers who are not allowed in China after they called for Quan’s expulsion.
Castro said it was difficult to pin blame on these officials.

“Hindi natin sila masisisi, dahil nakikita natin, ang bisita natin, bisita natin ay mukhang hindi itinuturing na maayos ang mismong nakatira sa bansang ito. So, doon sa mga opisyal na hindi na welcome sa China, itanong ninyo doon sa mga hindi welcome sa China, kung gusto ba nilang pumunta sa China,” Castro said.

(We cannot blame them, because we can see that our visitor, this visitor is not treating the residents of this country well. So, for the officials that are not welcome to China, you should ask them if they even want to go to China.) — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American taken captive by Russian forces years ago in Ukraine.

image.caption: Putin and Witkoff met in St. Petersburg for their ninth in-person talksImage: Kristina Solovyova/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the release of US captive Stephen Hubbard during talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on Wednesday.
Hubbard had been taken captive by Russian forces on charges of being a mercenary, which he denies. He was sentenced to seven years in prison at a closed trial in 2024.
Putin said Hubbard was at the airport and Witkoff said he was now "going home to his family."
US President Donald Trump later said that he had made the request directly to Putin during a phone call last week.

"The United States, out of respect for President Trump, was not required to give anything in return — an unprecedented situation for Russia," Trump claimed in a post on his Truth Social platform. "There was no 'swap' necessary for this release."

blocks.caption: A Russian court convicted Stephen Hubbard of being a mercenary in 2024, which he deniesImage: Moscow City Court press service/AFP

blocks.text: However, in a follow-up post, Trump also claimed that "numerous people" had called him to apologize after they criticized him for suspending a new round of sanctions, which he said was a necessary concession.
"If sanctions would have been placed, certainly those negotiations would have come to a complete and total halt," Trump's post said.
Putin, Witkoff to discuss Ukraine peace deal
The release of Hubbard was seen as a goodwill gesture to the Trump administreation as the two sides discuss a peace deal in Ukraine.
"We've brought some papers. It's really some ideas, some sort of peace deal between Russia and Ukraine, and you'll read that at your leisure," Witkoff told Putin.
Putin proposed that Witkoff discuss the restoration of bilateral ties between Washington and Moscow, and the possibility of trilateral talks with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing.

The meeting — the ninth such talks between Witkoff and Putin —comes a day after Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway, which US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as "positive."
"He will now, armed with those ideas, be able to ‌go to St. Petersburg and share them with the Russian side, and ‌let's ​see if we can make some progress," he said ahead of the talks.
Witkoff to return to Oslo
Witkoff's meeting with Zelenskyy and other European leaders in Oslo has brought fresh momentum to peace efforts, more than 4 years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The Ukrainian leader remained in Oslo on Wednesday where met with lawmakers in the Norwegian parliament.
Trump, Russia and Ukraine: Has the US changed sides again?
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said that Witkoff planned to return to Oslo for further consultations after his trip to St. Petersburg.
"I think we may have entered a phase now where the Russians are also looking for opportunities for diplomacy," he told Norway's public broadcaster NRK on Wednesday morning.
Nevertheless, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Moscow was willing to listen but that he didn't expect any "miracle." Trump on Tuesday reiterated that he wants Zelenskyy "to make a deal."

articles.title: UK approves Jackdaw gas field after years in limbo
articles.summary: Drilling is set to begin in the controversial North Sea plot as the government seeks to tackle high energy costs. Environmental groups have criticized the move and called for more clean energy.

image.caption: The Jackdaw gas field drilling venture had been approved by the Conservatives but held back by a Scottish courtImage: Adura/Handout/AFP

blocks.text: The UK government gave its approval for drilling to begin in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea on Wednesday following years of legal and political problems that had blocked the controversial fossil fuel venture.
The Labour government justified the move saying it would strengthen the UK's energy security amid rising energy costs due to the US-Israeli war against Iran.
The gas field had previously been approved by the previous Conservative government, but wes held up by a Scottish court that said the approval had failed to consider carbon emissions.
The field lies about 150 miles (240 kilometres) east of Aberdeen in Scotland.
What did the UK government say about the Jackdaw approval?

Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who has been under pressure from US President Donald Trump to increase drilling in the North Sea, said the new gas field would "protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm this winter."
"At a time when people are really struggling, it's right that we look in a responsible way at maximising the existing energy reserves we have in Britain that could help," he said.

"We're committed to moving towards renewable energy and reaching net zero by 2050. But even on our ambitious climate path, we'll still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come. That's why we're taking a pragmatic approach to the North Sea," Burnham added.

Energy Minister Miatta Fahnbulleh said gas could start flowing to British houses and businesses by the end of the month. It is expected that Jackdaw will increase domestic gas production by 6% and run for 11 years.
What has been the reaction to the UK's new gas project?
Shell, which is part of the Adura joint venture along with Norway's Equinor, welcomed the decision.
"Long-term energy projects depend on a competitive and stable investment environment, alongside timely and predictable regulatory decisions," Shell said.

However, the move has also been met with strong criticism. The Green Party called it "climate vandalism," while Greenpeace said the approval showed "the toxic grip fossil fuel lobbyists still hold over our energy policy."

"True pragmatism means severing our reliance on expensive oil and gas that leaves British households broke, supercharges extreme weather, and leaves our energy security at the mercy of petrostates," said the environmental group's Ami McCarthy.
Critics have also questioned whether the new project would indeed have an impact on British gas bills since prices are determined by global energy markets.

blocks.caption: Protesters had called on Burnham to block approval for the Jackdaw gas fieldImage: Henry Nicholls/AFP

blocks.text: In an attempt to show the government's commitment to its climate targets, alongside the Jackdaw approval, it announced the set up of a new Energy Wealth Fund, with an initial £2 billion ($2.7 billion), aimed at channeling oil and gas revenues into funding the transition to cleaner energy.

The UK is targeting net zero emissions by 2050, although this target must be examined under the realities already facing the planet, with a new UN report saying the world is heading for 2.8 degrees of warming, way beyond the 1.5 degrees target set in the Paris Climate Agreement.
It also comes after the UK experienced its hottest ever summer on record, with temperatures hitting previously unheard of 38 degrees in some areas in June, according to the Met Office.

articles.title: EXPLAINER: SC voids multi-trillion-peso budget laws in 2024 and 2025. Now what?
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has declared as unconstitutional the Philippines' national budget laws in 2024 and 2025 worth P5.768 trillion and P6.352 trillion respectively. It also struck down the provisions…

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 5:17pm
The Supreme Court has declared as unconstitutional the Philippines' national budget laws in 2024 and 2025 worth P5.768 trillion and P6.352 trillion respectively.
It also struck down the provisions allowing unprogrammed appropriations in the 2026 budget.
What happens now to the funds disbursed according to these laws and provisions?
In the case of allocations used in projects implemented in good faith, the funds need not be returned, the High Tribunal's spokesperson said on Wednesday.
At a press conference, Atty. Camille Ting said that the doctrine of operative fact applies.

“Under this doctrine, good faith projects already implemented and no longer reversible remain valid. Applying this doctrine, irreversible programs in the 2024 and 2025 GAAs whose beneficiaries acted in good faith are valid,” she said.
She later added, “there will be no funds returned in that case.”
Ting said Congress violated the Constitution when it increased the total appropriations submitted by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

When asked about Marcos’ accountability for signing the GAA, Ting said, "Accountability was not an issue in this case. The court did say that the author, implementor, or perpetrator of the unprogrammed appropriations that violate the constitution, they can be subject to civil criminal, or administrative liability."
"Liability is not an issue in this case. So what the Supreme Court just did was to determine whether the increase in programmed or unprogrammed funds were constitutional or not," Ting said.

However, she said the SC ruled that the author, implementor, or perpetrator of the unprogrammed appropriations that violate the Constitution, they can be subject to civil, criminal, or administrative liability, provided that they did not act in good faith.
When asked if the president may be considered an “implementor,” Ting said this will be on the discretion of the possible complainants.
“We do not know that. I mean it would depend on the case that’s filed and the evidence presented,” Ting said.
Motion for reconsideration
Ting said the case is also not yet final and may be appealed.
“It will always be subject of a motion for reconsideration. They are given 15 days to file their motion for consideration from notice of the decision,” she said.
Earlier, Malacañang said that it will ask the SC to reconsider its ruling through the Office of the Solicitor General.
Meanwhile, Ting stressed that unprogrammed appropriations are not unconstitutional, per se.
“They’re allowed as long as it’s within the guidelines,” she said. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Over 8,000 endangered golden-crowned flying foxes recorded in Aurora
articles.summary: More than 8,000 golden-crowned flying foxes, an endangered species of fruit bat, were observed in a roosting site in Aurora Memorial National Park (AMNP), the Department of Environment and Natural…

More than 8,000 golden-crowned flying foxes, an endangered species of fruit bat, were observed in a roosting site in Aurora Memorial National Park (AMNP), the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Central Luzon said.
The bats were observed during DENR’s monitoring activity. This was the second time that such fruit bat species were observed at the roosting site, the department said.

blocks.caption: Photo from DENR-Central Luzon

“Protecting the roosting sites and feeding habitats of this fruit bat species is essential to sustaining ecological functions and maintaining the health of Aurora’s vast forest ecosystems,” said DENR Maria Aurora community head Marivic Santos in a statement.
